actions.justification: Mandatory first step — establish baseline hemodynamic and respiratory status to guide severity assessment and triage.
Mandatory assessment of respiratory function (work of breathing, oxygen requirement, auscultation) to characterize the pulmonary presentation and guide management.
Mandatory chest X-ray to identify infiltrates, consolidation, effusion, or other findings that confirm pneumonia or suggest alternative diagnoses in this immunocompromised patient.
MANDATORY action - CBC required within 60 minutes to assess white cell count, anemia, and thrombocytopenia, critical in this immunosuppressed patient with suspected pneumonia.
CURB-65 score guides pneumonia severity classification and helps determine appropriate level of care and treatment intensity for this CAP patient.
Blood cultures should be obtained BEFORE antibiotic administration per IDSA CAP guidelines, especially important in immunosuppressed patients at higher risk for bacteremia.
Immunocompromised patient with pneumonia symptoms requires ICU criteria assessment to determine appropriate level of care and guide disposition decisions per CAP/IDSA guidelines.

Procalcitonin helps differentiate bacterial from viral/fungal pneumonia, guides antibiotic therapy decisions, and is particularly valuable in immunosuppressed patients where the clinical picture may be atypical.
Urinary Legionella antigen is recommended in CAP workup, especially in immunocompromised patients where atypical pathogens are more prevalent and require different antibiotic coverage.

Immunocompromised patient with CAP presentation - sputum culture is indicated to identify causative organism and guide antibiotic therapy, especially important in immunosuppressed patients who may harbor atypical or opportunistic pathogens. Not yet completed.

Basic metabolic panel to assess renal function (important for antibiotic dosing), electrolytes, and glucose - relevant for this immunosuppressed patient with respiratory illness and to complete severity assessment.

Patient with cough, fever, dyspnea and immunosuppression with pending labs — empiric coverage for community-acquired pneumonia with beta-lactam plus macrolide is appropriate per IDSA/ATS CAP guidelines. Immunocompromised patients are at higher risk and benefit from early empiric antibiotic therapy. All key diagnostics (cultures, CXR, labs) have already been ordered, so antibiotics can now be initiated without further delay.
IV fluid administration is supportive care for a febrile patient with pneumonia/respiratory illness to maintain hydration and hemodynamic stability, particularly in an immunosuppressed host.

Patient is immunosuppressed with CAP (cough, fever, dyspnea). Beta-lactam plus macrolide already initiated. Adding a respiratory fluoroquinolone provides broader coverage including atypical organisms and is indicated in immunocompromised CAP patients per IDSA/ATS guidelines as an alternative or adjunctive regimen. This is the only available action in the current phase.
Immunocompromised patient with cough, fever, dyspnea — PCP (Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia) must be excluded as it is a common opportunistic infection in this population.

Serial reassessment is indicated to monitor for clinical deterioration or improvement following empiric antibiotic therapy in this immunocompromised patient with CAP/atypical/opportunistic pneumonia presentation.
Continuous SpO2 monitoring is essential in a patient with respiratory illness and immunosuppression to detect early deterioration requiring escalation of care or supplemental oxygen.
Multiple labs are pending (CBC, BMP, procalcitonin, PCP workup, blood/sputum cultures). Reviewing results as they return will guide diagnosis refinement and targeted therapy adjustments.
Immunocompromised patient with PCP workup pending — HIV status should be confirmed as it directly affects management (e.g., PCP prophylaxis dosing, opportunistic infection risk stratification).
Immunocompromised patient with pulmonary infiltrates/symptoms warrants fungal workup (galactomannan, beta-D-glucan, cryptococcal antigen) to evaluate for opportunistic fungal pneumonia.

Serial vital sign monitoring is essential in immunocompromised patients with pneumonia to detect early clinical deterioration, particularly worsening hypoxia, tachycardia, or fever recurrence, which would trigger ICU escalation.
Reassessing oxygenation and respiratory status at 100 minutes ensures ongoing adequacy of SpO2 and breathing effort, guiding need for supplemental oxygen or escalation of respiratory support.

Chest X-ray was ordered as part of initial workup. Reviewing results now will help identify consolidation patterns, interstitial infiltrates (PCP), cavitation (fungal), or other findings that guide targeted therapy in this immunocompromised patient.

Patient has received beta-lactam+macrolide and respiratory fluoroquinolone; with now stable vitals at 115 minutes, reassess treatment response to guide further management including need for PCP-specific therapy (TMP-SMX) given immunosuppression and pending fungal/PCP workup.
